8b207487493976ecf18e.en: Newtalk News aimed at the long-term photography policy often promoted by Tsai Ing-wen's government. Zhang Jingsen, a former member of the Executive Yuan, criticized today (3) that Taiwan's population is aging by millions, but Taiwan's accommodation-type long-term photography-related institutions have only added 12,971 beds in the six years from 2018 to 2024, with a growth rate of only 12.3%. The government currently plans to add only about 7,000 more beds by 2028. He said that it would be better to use 10,000 yuan per capita to set up additional care institutions. Zhang Jingsen said on Facebook that being elderly in Taiwan is not the same as being elderly at home: it's time for Taiwan's long-term photo policy to take a turn! In the past decade, Taiwan's long-term care policy has emphasized "local eldercare" and invested a lot of resources in the development of home services, daylight centers and community care. This direction is not wrong in itself. The problem is that the policy has been implemented so far, and gradually narrowed down "local elders" to "elders at home".
